plain: The sudden boom in research on Einstein's theory of gravity in the 1950s and 60s, known as the golden age of general relativity, makes no sense on its face, according to the researcher Eric Weinstein. He says it is really a story about two men, Agnew Bahnson and Roger Babson, and he starts to describe what they appear to have been before his sentence breaks off. He raises it because, to him, it hints that someone was quietly pushing gravity research forward.
